Hi Adeeb,

Here are our thoughts on the incentive structure. Please use following commentary for your call with Dr Joshua on Sunday evening Panama time. Once done, we should also send him an email to document this. I can do that once we speak on Monday morning, after your call with him.

Goal is to achieve 2,500 grafts in a single day over a period of 6 months and therefore both “speed” and “quality” are equally important parameters to measure performance.

Following structure will be applicable from March 1 - June 30, 2022 and will be reassessed during next cycle of 4 months.


1.     Hair transplant

  *   >1,500 grafts
     *   Incentive will be 2.5% of sales (net of tax) subject to achievement of average extraction speed of at least 500 grafts per hour and ratio of 1.85
     *   Incentive will be 5% of sales (net of tax) subject to achievement of average extraction speed of at least 500 grafts per hour and ratio of 2.0
  *   1,250 - 1,500 grafts – 2.5% of sales (net of tax) subject to achievement of average extraction speed of at least 500 grafts per hour and ratio above 2.0
  *   Less than 1,250 grafts - No incentives
  *

2.    Eyebrows – No incentives.


3.     Beard

  *   Patchy beard (top-up) (grafts up to 1,500) – no incentives
  *   Full beard (>1,500 grafts)
     *   If implants are 7.5% more than committed numbers – Incentive will be 2.5% of sales (net of tax)
     *   If implants are 15% more than committed numbers – Incentive will be 5% of sales (net of tax)
     *

4.     Special cases – Based on size and difficulty. To be discussed before booking and expectations set.

Over and above, an extra special fixed bonus of $1,250 will be provided for performing 14 sessions in a month. For every session beyond 14, there will be an extra special fixed bonus of $300 for each session. However, if more than 1 surgery is cancelled due to the doctor, no incentive will be provided in that month.

For sake of clarity, February fee will be paid at 15% flat.

Regards
Harsh/ Paul

ATPv

ATPv is our additive to graft holding solutions made from our patented
formulation of liposomes containing adenosine triphosphate. 

 

Use Instructions

When using ATPv, the solution should be diluted into your graft holding
solution (i.e. Saline, Hypothermosol, Plasmalyte A). We recommend a 10%
dilution. For example, each 50 cc bottle can be added to 450 cc holding
solution. 

 

We recommend if you are doing FUE cases to order the 25-cc ATPv bottles, and
for FUT cases to order the 50-cc ATPv bottles. One bottle is enough for one
surgery. The product is sterile filled therefore should not be reused once
opened.

 

We also recommend that you assess your case load for the upcoming weeks and
plan accordingly so that you can most accurately order ATPv with regards to
the shelf life of 66 days.

 

Storage Instructions

The ATPv solution should be stored in the refrigerator until the day of use

Hi team,

Firstly, thank you for all your amazing effort over the last few weeks. I know it's hard at times, especially with the long sessions. We really appreciate you and your expertise.

This whole covid situation has thrown another curve ball, with the border remaining closed for at least the month of Feb, my planned return to clinic is being postponed once again.

But now that the team is getting quicker at setting up the surgery, as well as the actual sessions themselves, I believe we should be implementing staggered starts and finishes, making sure no one is working excessively long days.

Having worked in many surgeries globally, what generally works best is that one of our RN nurses open and set up, start the surgery for the day, but finishes around 4.30pm/5pm. The other Nurse/nurses to start later 9.30am, and to finish the day with the post op and clean. If the surgery goes beyond 6pm, the following day, they can start later around 10.30am.

In surgery we should only have 2 nurses at any one time, as space is scarce and whom ever is out of surgery can work with Karen on the patients pre ops etc. Over the next couple of weeks, advertising for our other treatments will start and training will need to be provided on PRP and Mesotherapy. This will provide a nice break from surgery and offer more variety to your day. We hope to also start injectable, vampire face lifts and IV clinic in the very near future as well.

I hope this makes sense and please do not hesitate to contact me or Karen if you need more information and any suggestions.

Also, Karen is going to start keeping track of extra hours worked (TOIL) and what you have already, so that when we stagger the start/finish times and since we have 3 nurses, I can ask someone to go home early, start later, day off etc to use up TOIL (if you are all happy with that).

With most Zaps, the action happens right after the trigger. But what if you
don't want your action to happen immediately?

 With Delay by Zapier <https://zapier.com/apps/delay?utm_content=body>, you
can postpone any action step of a Zap until you want it to happen. Check out
our video to learn more about how Delay can give you more flexibility with your

 Watch the video
<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zKlZNCwiDdw&list=PLqzJRGwum4KMoJdVeW2z_qFLGe3Wl6Xo4&index=14>
What can Delay do?



Delay for
Delay an action for a designated time interval (like 1 hour or 7 days)







Delay until
Delay an action until a specific date or time.







Delay after queue
Advanced version of "Delay for". Create a queue of actions and set the time
that you want each item to wait before it continues. This option only appears
when you have an existing Delay step in your Zap.
